span.p: Does it hold/process production customer data or PII?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Production access or a critical dependency?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Tier 1 - critical: full SIG/CAIQ + a real read of the SOC 2/ISO scope, period, exceptions, CUECs

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Tier 2 - moderate: SIG-Lite + the vendor's current attestation + CUEC mapping

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Any access to internal systems or non-public data?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Tier 3 - low: lightweight attestation on file; re-confirm at renewal

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Clean opinion but exceptions in YOUR critical control area?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Not assurance - treat the exception as a residual risk you own + implement your CUECs

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Rely + monitor; map every CUEC to a control you evidence; set a tier-driven re-assessment cadence
